newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria state-run firms register 9-mth losses.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria state-run firms register 9-mth losses.

text.p: Of the 1,160 enterprises supervised by Bulgaria's industry ministry, 401 registered losses for the first nine months in 1996, interim industry minister Alexander Bozhkov said on Monday.
He told a news conference their debts totalled 377 billion levs and said crisis-ridden Bulgaria was the only East European country to report a drop in production in 1996.
Bozhkov said the ministry's main priority under his leadership would be the liquidation of loss-making firms and the fight against corruption.

"My opinion, which has been shared by the World Bank, is that fixing a list of enterprises to be liquidated is not the best approach. It's more important to liquidate a certain percentage of the state assets and to liquidate those which register losses," Bozhkov said.
Bozhkov said there had been complaints from German investors about biased tender procedures and the new leadership was eager to implement strict rules.

The previous ministry chiefs signed many deals during their last days in office and many of them will be revised, ministry officials said. They said seven deals were signed on February 12, the former administration's final day in power.

The International Monetary Fund suspended new lending last year because of the former Socialist government's failure to meet reform targets including closure of loss-making state enterprises and privatisation.
The caretaker cabinet took office on February 13 and will govern until after general elections on April 19. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
